newsitem.title: USA: CME debt products extend open interest record.
newsitem.headline: CME debt products extend open interest record.

text.p: Total open interest in interest-rate products traded on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange hit a record high for the ninth consecutive day on Wednesday, the exchange said Thursday.
Open interest in the debt futures and options contracts totalled 6,112,146 contracts at end of Wednesday's business, adding about 50,000 to Tuesday's record, a CME spokesman said.
CME's exchange-wide open interest had also made new highs during most of that nine-day period from May 30, standing at a record 7,697,801 contracts on Wednesday, he added.
Leo Melamed, CME chairman emeritus and senior policy adviser, said in a statement that improvements in the exchange's flagship Eurodollar contracts contributed to the increased activity.

"The enhancements of adding half-ticks to Eurodollar futures and expanding the product base to include mid-curve options have made these products more appealing to our customers," Melamed said in a statement.
Of the total open interest, Eurodollar futures accounted for 2,838,132 contracts and options on those futures 3,170,500 contracts, the exchange said.

CME earlier this year halved the minimum price unit to one-half basis point (0.005 point) from one basis point (0.01) previously. Mid-curve options are options that expire in the near months but are based on futures expiring in those months of the next year or the year after.
